correctness.rationale: With Fourier multipliers (0,1,2,2,1), Parseval gives energy S+z² for u=a+x+y, where a=sqrt(1-S), S=||x||²+||y||², and z=||y|| for the second harmonic. Expansion of u² log(u²) gives deficit 2z²-2<x²y>-2<xy²>+< (x+y)^4 >/6+S²/2+O(S^(5/2)); the separate third moments vanish. In this real five-point Fourier decomposition ||P₂(x²)||=||x||²/sqrt(2) and <x⁴>=3||x||⁴/2. If z/S tends to infinity, the quadratic term dominates the numerator on the S² denominator scale. Consequently finite liminf sequences can be restricted to z=O(S), on which the pure first-harmonic quartic term gives 3S²/4 together with the normalization correction. The estimate reduces to 2z²-sqrt(2)Sz+3S²/4=2(z-S/(2sqrt(2)))²+S²/2. The displayed cosine path saturates the inequality because its second harmonic has the optimal norm and phase. Thus the exact local limit is 1/2. I independently computed the witness using integer cyclic correlations combined with Parseval, and exact rational enclosures of the entropy using the range-reduced -log(1-t) series. Its ratio is in (0.472467667182636,0.472467667182637), with exact rational comparison to 19/40. A neighborhood of 1 has quotient exceeding the witness; its compact admissible complement contains a global minimizer by continuity, even if some entries are zero.
residual_risks: The witness is not asserted to be optimal; the precise infimum and the form and uniqueness of minimizers remain unknown.
